text:
incident-bot: [PAGER] latency.p99 > 1200ms for streaming-inference-prod across us-west-2 nodes. Paging oncall.

Maya Patel: oncall here — investigating. seeing p95 rising too. starting with routing and GPU fleet dashboards. @Jon / @Priya ping if you are online.

Jon Kim: on it. I see a cluster of thermal warnings on node gpu-23 and gpu-27 in rack-a3. `nvidia-smi` shows elevated temps and a stream of correctable ECC errors.

Priya Rao: I can take telemetry. attaching flamegraph for kv-cache lookups — appears normal. this smells like hardware throttling not software regression.

Yang Zhao: CPU and network look fine. streaming worker latency spikes align with bursts from pod-controllers that rescheduled onto gpu-23. possibly noisy neighbor + thermal.

Maya Patel: quick mitigation — can we reroute new streaming sessions off the problematic hosts and scale up warm spares? priority is to keep p99 < 800ms.

Jon Kim: doing a rolling drain of gpu-23 and gpu-27. command:
```
kubectl drain node/gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl cordon node/gpu-27
```
will also trigger fallback routing.

deploy-bot: Canary fallback policy applied: routing streaming requests -> model-variant redwood-raft-quantized-v2 on dedicated-pool-b until capacity stabilizes.

Maya Patel: update: tail stalls reduced but still seeing intermittent p99 blips. streaming chunk stalls at ~7s for a subset of sessions. logs show `nvlink timeout` around the same timestamps.

Jon Kim: found kernel-level ECC correctable error counters increasing. I recommend pulling the nodes for hardware repro and migrating workloads. marking node gpu-23 as degraded: `node-status: thermal-ecc-degraded`.

infra-bot: Node gpu-23 flagged: thermal threshold exceeded 2x in 10m; ECC-correctable-errors high. Auto-quarantine initiated.

Priya Rao: Customer impact estimate: ~3.8% of streaming requests in US-WEST-2 experienced p99 > 2s for a 12m window. Embeddings and non-streaming gen unaffected.

Amy Chen: Support notified top 5 customers on the affected region via status page and DM. TICKET-2024-874 created for external comms.

Yang Zhao: Mitigation steps in order:
1) Quarantine gpu-23/gpu-27 (done)
2) Reroute streaming traffic to warm spares (deploy-bot did)
3) Increase batching timeout for streaming-lite to avoid stalls (patch rolling out)
4) Add temporary 5% extra capacity in dedicated pool

Maya Patel: rolling patch to increase streaming-lite `max_chunk_wait_ms` from `50` -> `120` to reduce tail stalls. CI passed. rolling to canary now.

Jon Kim: hardware ops scheduled for node inspection. leaving nodes quarantined until on-prem team verifies. pushing recovery to next hour.

Priya Rao: monitoring: p95 back within SLO, p99 at ~950ms now, down from 1.6s. continued watch.

Maya Patel: good. action items:
- Jon: coordinate hardware handoff and post-mortem (assign)
- Priya: collect precise ingest ids for affected sessions for offline evals
- Amy: outbound comms draft (ETA ~30m)

Jon Kim: ack. I'll open HW-REQ-462 and timeline the takeover.

deploy-bot: Fallback model traffic now 18% of total streaming for us-west-2. No regression alerts.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated — emergency routing and node quarantine reduced customer impact. Incident status: monitoring. Escalation: SEV3 -> SEV2 handled. If stable for 30m, will close.

Amy Chen: posted status update on status.redwood.ai and pinged enterprise accounts.

Maya Patel: leaving handoff to night shift. tagging @Yang for overnight watch. Thanks all — parallel follow-ups in ops-docs will capture runbook changes.

Yang Zhao: I'll watch the dashboards and confirm stability. thumbs up :thumbsup:

Maya Patel: incident closed: nodes quarantined and workloads migrated. postmortem to follow with timeline and root cause hypothesis: thermal-triggered ECC flurries causing intermittent nvlink stalls leading to streaming tail latency. Thanks everyone.

incident-bot: Incident resolved. Duration: 00:42:53. Severity: SEV2 -> Resolved.
